Claim 0: Fresnel presented his lighthouse lens in 1822. Supported in a corrected form: Fresnel designed the lens and it was officially tested in 1822 (20 August 1822, Arc de Triomphe); the first lighthouse Fresnel lens was lit in 1823 at Cordouan.
- Wikipedia, Fresnel lens: official test on 20 August 1822 witnessed from 20 miles away; first lighthouse Fresnel lens lit 25 July 1823. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fresnel_lens
- Dunkirk Lighthouse: In 1822 a French physicist, Augustin Fresnel, invented the lens. Source: https://dunkirklighthouse.com/fresnel__lens_history.htm
- IEEE Spectrum and NPS: in 1822 Augustin-Jean Fresnel invented a new type of lens that produced a much stronger beam. Source: https://spectrum.ieee.org/fresnel-lens-milestone
- Guinness: first Fresnel lens in a lighthouse, Cordouan 1823. Source: https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/717348-first-fresnel-lens-in-a-lighthouse

Claim 1: a first-order Fresnel lens beam could be seen about 20 miles out to sea. Supported as written.
- NPS Cape Hatteras: the first-order lens, used primarily as a seacoast light, its beam is visible over twenty miles out to sea. Source: https://www.nps.gov/caha/learn/historyculture/fresnellens.htm
- Smithsonian Magazine: the first Fresnel lens was visible to the horizon, more than 20 miles away. Source: https://www.smithsonianmag.com/science-nature/science-makes-a-better-lighthouse-lens-170677431/

Claim 2: big rotating lenses floated on a mercury bath to turn with little friction. Supported as written.
- US Lighthouse Society: lenses floated on a mercury bath; lenses weighing several tons could be started with a single finger; workable system by Bourdelles around 1890. Source: https://uslhs.org/node/1614
- STLE, Mercurial bearing. Source: https://www.stle.org/files/TLTArchives/2015/04_April/From_the_Editor.aspx
